Definition: {properly, to plough, or (generally) break forth, i.e. (figuratively) to inspect, admire, care for, consider}
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible beqar means to search, to inquire, and it appears 5 times across the Bible. Ezra's enemies urge the king to search the records, and the search is made in the house of the rolls.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the truth stands up to searching — the king's search found Cyrus's decree, and honest inquiry still finds God's word true. That is why I keep coming back to it: beqar is not a word to rush past.
